summary: Tony Walter is a religious studies scholar. He studied at Durham University (BA, 1967–1970) and the University of Aberdeen (PhD, 1970–1975). He held posts at Aberdeen, Reading (1994–2006), and the University of Bath (Professor 2006, Emeritus since 2015).

Torakazu Doi (1902–1971) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe (~1923–1926) and later held posts at Sagami Women's University (~1953–1964) and Dokkyo University (~1964–1971).

Torkel Brekke works in religious studies, Indology, and history. He studied at the University of Oslo (MPhil under Jens Braarvig and Georg von Simson) and Oxford (DPhil under Richard Gombrich). He held posts at Oslo, PRIO, OsloMet, and MF Norwegian School of Theology.

Toru Funayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner (1991–1992). He held posts at Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019) and Kyushu University (attested 1999–2003).

Toru Haneda (1882–1955) worked in Sinology, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the Third Higher School, University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. His career included long-standing positions at Kyoto University (1909–1945), its Institute for Research in Humanities, and Toho Gakkai.

Toru Kumeji specializes in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He has held posts at the Center for Open Humanities Data and as chief researcher at the Humanities Information Studies Institute (attested 2015).

Toru Sagara (1921–2000) was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1941–1944) and held posts at Ibaraki University (~1949–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University (~1982–1992).

Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) worked in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Fourth Higher School and University of Tokyo. His main appointments included posts at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Dongguk University (1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne (D. Litt.). He held appointments at Lausanne, IKGA, the Humanities Information Studies Institute, and the Center for Open Humanities Data.
Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University from around 1966 to 1970 and later held an academic post there from approximately 1988 to 2018.

Toshifumi Goto is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1982, studying under several scholars including Karl Hoffmann. He has held professorships at Osaka University and Tohoku University (attested 2003–2005).
Toshihide Unebe is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Issai Funahashi. He held an appointment as professor at Doho University (attested 1991).

Toshihiko Izutsu (1914–1993) worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. Educated at Keio University (1931–1937), he taught there from 1937 to 1981, and later held posts at McGill University (1961, 1969–1975) and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (1975–1979).

Toshihiko Kimura works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963) and held posts at Tohoku University, Tokai Gakuin University (~1978–1987), and Shitennoji University (~2011).
Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981 and served as a professor at Nagoya University (~1988–2020).

Toshiichi Endo works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (PhD, 1995), supervised by Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake, and also studied under Hajime Nakamura and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha.

Toshikazu Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held research positions at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011–2015) and IKGA, and became a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

Toshiki Osada specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Hokkaido University (~1973–1977) and held posts at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1993–2003) and the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2020).

Toshinori Ochiai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held posts at Kacho Junior College (~1983–1996), the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1996), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2019), and the Institute for the Study of Ancient Manuscript Buddhist Canons (~2007).
Toshio Ando (1909–1973) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1930 to 1933 and held posts at Doho University and Otani University (~1950–1973).
